prompt.brief: Design a multi-cloud FinOps platform that normalizes billing and usage, allocates costs, detects waste/anomalies, recommends rightsizing or commitments, and forecasts spend with explainable evidence.
successSignals: Define normalized billing line items, usage/resource identity, ownership/tag policy, allocation rules, commitments, recommendations, and realized savings.
Reconcile provider invoices with usage, handle credits/taxes/currency, delayed data, shared resources, and changing prices without hiding uncertainty.
Separate ingestion and normalization from dashboards, forecasting, recommendation computation, approval workflows, and provider-side changes.
Explain recommendation safety, stale billing, privacy/tenant isolation, auditability, feedback, observability, and degraded reporting.

functional: Ingest multi-cloud billing/usage data, normalize resources and currencies, allocate shared spend, and expose daily/monthly cost views.
Detect anomalies and idle resources, forecast spend, recommend rightsizing/commitments, model scenarios, and track approved savings.
Support budgets/alerts, showback/chargeback, recommendation approval, provider action rollback where possible, corrections, and audit exports.
nonFunctional: Publish cost data within 24 hours of provider availability and show recommendation confidence, assumptions, and expected savings.
Process billions of billing line items across providers without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 1B billing line items/month across 10k accounts and 3 cloud providers
Partition raw and normalized data by tenant, provider, account, and billing period; shard large accounts and hot shared services.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

metrics.label: Peak scale
metrics.description: Capacity assumption that drives partitioning and backpressure.

metrics.label: Latency target
metrics.description: Interactive spend and recommendation reads are served from projections; every result carries its source and projection watermark.

metrics.label: Durable boundary
metrics.description: Provider billing records and approved allocation rules are authoritative; forecasts and recommendations are derived.

metrics.label: Async boundary
metrics.description: Keep billing ingestion, allocation, forecasting, anomaly detection, rightsizing, commitment analysis, and index refresh off the synchronous path.

entities.name: BillingLineItem
entities.notes: Immutable provider evidence kept with source identifiers, credits, taxes, rate context, and collection watermark so invoice totals can be reconciled.

entities.name: ResourceOwnership
entities.notes: Versioned mapping used for showback and chargeback; unknown ownership is surfaced as unallocated.

entities.name: CostSnapshot
entities.notes: Serving aggregate keyed by account and period with allocation coverage and provider watermark.

entities.name: OptimizationRecommendation
entities.notes: Versioned explainable candidate for idle cleanup, rightsizing, or commitment purchase.

apis.contract: { provider, accountId, credentialsRef, billingSource, ownerMapping } -> { connectionId, status, firstImportJobId }
apis.notes: Create a tenant-scoped connector without storing provider secrets in the application and start asynchronous backfill.

apis.contract: { totals[], trends[], allocationCoverage, sourceWatermark, projectionWatermark, freshness }
apis.notes: Return authorized allocated and unallocated cost without implying stale data is final.

apis.contract: { items: [{ id, type, evidence, savings, confidence, status }], nextCursor, generatedAt }
apis.notes: Filter explainable recommendations by owner, provider, account, type, and lifecycle status.

apis.contract: { recommendationVersion, decision, actorId, idempotencyKey } -> { actionId, status, expiresAt }
apis.notes: Recheck freshness, policy, role, savings evidence, and provider preconditions; reject stale approvals.

dataFlow.title: Connect cloud accounts and collect evidence
dataFlow.description: Provider adapters use scoped credentials and provider cursors to land billing exports, usage, rates, credits, and resource inventory while respecting provider quotas.

dataFlow.title: Preserve raw billing and reconcile invoices
dataFlow.description: The billing lake keeps immutable provider-native partitions; reconciliation compares invoice totals, credits, taxes, and exchange-rate inputs before a period is marked complete.

dataFlow.title: Normalize and allocate cost
dataFlow.description: Workers convert line items to a canonical model, apply amortization and currency rules, join effective ownership, and publish explicit unallocated spend for missing metadata.

dataFlow.title: Detect waste and generate explainable recommendations
dataFlow.description: Feature workers build utilization and spend windows; forecasting, anomaly, idle-resource, rightsizing, and commitment models produce evidence-backed candidates.

dataFlow.title: Review, execute, and measure savings
dataFlow.description: Policy rules and user approval gate mutations; the executor performs guarded provider actions and later compares billing and usage with the baseline.

architecture.title: Multi-cloud FinOps and cost intelligence reference architecture
architecture.summary: Provider billing exports and resource inventories are retained as immutable, tenant-partitioned evidence. A normalization pipeline joins usage, rates, tags, and ownership; forecasting, anomaly detection, rightsizing, and commitment analysis produce explainable recommendations. A policy and approval boundary keeps risky provider actions human-controlled while the serving index exposes current spend, savings evidence, and forecast freshness quickly.

layers.label: FinOps user and control plane
layers.description: FinOps teams query spend, configure allocation and savings policies, review recommendations, and approve provider changes through an authenticated API.

layers.label: Multi-cloud billing and inventory ingestion
layers.description: Provider adapters pull billing exports, usage details, rates, and resource metadata without allowing one provider's throttling to block the rest of the platform.

layers.label: Cost intelligence and recommendation plane
layers.description: Normalized line items are allocated to owners, enriched with utilization history, and evaluated by forecasting, anomaly, waste, rightsizing, and commitment models under versioned policy.

layers.label: Recommendation, approval, and action plane
layers.description: Durable recommendation decisions are indexed for dashboards and can become idempotent, auditable actions only after approval and provider-specific safety checks.

layers.label: FinOps data quality and safety operations
layers.description: Freshness, allocation coverage, forecast error, savings realization, model drift, provider failures, approval safety, and replay parity are monitored per tenant and account.

keyPaths.label: Spend and recommendation query path
keyPaths.description: FinOps console -> gateway -> cost API -> serving index, returning account, service, tag, forecast, and recommendation freshness metadata.

keyPaths.label: Provider data ingestion path
keyPaths.description: Cloud provider adapters -> billing lake and resource catalog -> event bus -> cost normalizer, with provider cursors, rate limits, and late-data handling.

keyPaths.label: Explainable recommendation path
keyPaths.description: Normalized usage -> feature history -> optimization engine -> policy engine -> recommendation store -> serving index.

keyPaths.label: Approved savings action path
keyPaths.description: FinOps approval -> policy engine -> action executor -> provider adapter, with an audit record, dry-run result, rollback guard, and notification for every attempted change.

components.label: FinOps console and integrations
components.description: Cloud finance, platform, and engineering users inspect spend by account, service, owner, tag, and time window; review evidence and approve recommendations.

properties.protocol: HTTPS dashboard, webhook, and export clients

components.label: Tenant and account API gateway
components.description: Authenticates users and cloud connectors, isolates tenants and accounts, enforces query and export quotas, and validates approval idempotency keys.

properties.protection: Tenant/account authorization, quotas, and idempotent approvals

components.label: Spend and recommendation API
components.description: Serves spend rollups, forecasts, anomalies, recommendation evidence, and freshness metadata; routes policy changes and approval requests to the control plane.

properties.contract: Tenant-scoped spend, forecast, recommendation, and approval APIs

components.label: Cloud provider adapters
components.description: Isolates AWS, Azure, and GCP credentials and API semantics; fetches billing exports, usage, rates, resource inventory, and executes only approved provider changes.

properties.providers: AWS CUR, Azure Cost Management, GCP Billing export, provider APIs

components.label: Raw billing and usage lake
components.description: Retains immutable provider line items, credits, taxes, rates, exchange-rate inputs, collection cursors, and source timestamps for replay and reconciliation.

properties.partitioning: Tenant, provider, account, billing period, and ingestion date

components.label: Resource, tag, and ownership catalog
components.description: Maps provider resource IDs to services, environments, teams, business units, tags, regions, and lifecycle state so costs can be allocated consistently.

properties.consistency: Versioned account/resource mappings with effective timestamps

components.label: Cost data event bus
components.description: Publishes billing batch accepted, inventory updated, normalized cost ready, recommendation created, approval recorded, and action completed events with replayable offsets.

properties.delivery: At least once; partition by tenant/account and deduplicate by source event

components.label: Cost normalization and allocation
components.description: Converts provider-specific line items into a canonical cost model, applies currency and amortization rules, joins resource ownership, and marks unallocated or late data explicitly.

properties.guarantee: Deterministic, replayable transforms with source lineage and allocation coverage

components.label: Usage history and feature store
components.description: Stores time-windowed spend, utilization, seasonality, commitment coverage, idle-resource signals, and feature snapshots keyed by account and resource.

properties.retention: Daily and hourly history with model-versioned feature snapshots

components.label: Forecast, anomaly, and savings engine
components.description: Runs spend forecasts and anomaly detection, identifies idle resources and rightsizing candidates, and evaluates reserved-instance or savings-plan scenarios with confidence and evidence.

properties.outputs: Forecast bands, anomaly scores, utilization evidence, savings estimate, and model version

components.label: Savings policy and approval engine
components.description: Applies tenant budgets, minimum confidence, savings thresholds, environment exclusions, commitment risk limits, approval roles, and fail-safe action rules.

properties.safety: Human approval for mutations; dry-run and rollback checks before provider execution

components.label: Recommendation and audit store
components.description: Stores versioned recommendations, evidence references, savings estimates, confidence, policy decision, approval history, action status, and immutable audit records.

properties.consistency: Optimistic versioning and idempotent recommendation/action transitions

components.label: Spend and recommendation serving index
components.description: Indexes allocated spend, trends, forecasts, anomalies, recommendation status, savings evidence, and freshness by tenant, account, resource, owner, and time range.

properties.latency: Interactive FinOps dashboard queries with projection watermark and stale-data banner

components.label: Approved action executor
components.description: Revalidates policy and provider state, performs dry runs, executes rightsizing or commitment changes with bounded retries, and records idempotent outcomes for rollback review.

properties.guarantee: No mutation without approval, current policy, provider precondition, and audit record

components.label: FinOps notification service
components.description: Notifies owners about anomalies, budget risk, recommendation expiry, approval requests, and completed or failed actions through configured channels.

properties.delivery: Deduplicated email, chat, webhook, and ticket notifications

components.label: FinOps quality and safety observability
components.description: Tracks provider ingestion freshness, missing accounts, allocation coverage, unallocated spend, forecast error, savings realization, model drift, queue lag, action failures, and approval bypass attempts.

properties.alerts: Stale billing, reconciliation gaps, quality regressions, provider throttling, and unsafe action signals

connections.label: Spend query or approval request
connections.description: The console submits tenant-scoped spend queries, connector setup, recommendation reviews, and approval decisions over authenticated HTTPS.

connections.label: Authorized FinOps request
connections.description: The gateway validates tenant, account, role, time range, export quota, and approval idempotency before routing the request.

connections.label: Spend and recommendation read
connections.description: The API reads pre-aggregated spend, forecasts, anomalies, and recommendation evidence with projection watermark and source freshness.

connections.label: Recommendation review or approval
connections.description: A user review or approval is checked against the current recommendation version and sent to policy evaluation; stale approvals are rejected.

connections.label: Raw billing and usage export
connections.description: Adapters land provider-native line items, credits, rates, and collection metadata before any normalization, preserving source lineage for reconciliation.

connections.label: Resource inventory sync
connections.description: Adapters upsert provider resources, tags, accounts, regions, and lifecycle state with effective timestamps and a provider cursor.

connections.label: Billing batch accepted
connections.description: A durable manifest event announces each accepted billing partition and source watermark so downstream consumers can replay or backfill it.

connections.label: Inventory mapping updated
connections.description: Versioned ownership and tag changes are published for allocation recomputation without rewriting the raw provider export.

connections.label: Normalize and allocate work
connections.description: Partitioned workers consume billing and inventory events at least once, deduplicate source manifests, and retry provider-independent transforms safely.

connections.label: Effective ownership mapping
connections.description: Normalization joins each line item to the resource and tag mapping valid at the usage timestamp, marking unknown ownership instead of guessing.

connections.label: Canonical cost history
connections.description: Canonical spend, utilization, allocation, and rate features are written with source lineage, currency, amortization mode, and processing watermark.

connections.label: Time-windowed features
connections.description: The intelligence workers read bounded history and feature snapshots to forecast spend, detect spikes, identify waste, and model rightsizing or commitment scenarios.

connections.label: Explainable savings candidate
connections.description: The engine submits a candidate with evidence, confidence, forecast interval, estimated savings, risk, model version, and provider preconditions.

connections.label: Policy decision and audit
connections.description: Policy records recommend, defer, suppress, or require-approval decisions with the rule version and immutable evidence references.

connections.label: Dashboard projection
connections.description: Projection workers index recommendation lifecycle, savings evidence, action status, and freshness alongside allocated spend for fast filtering.

connections.label: Approved action intent
connections.description: Only a current, approved, policy-compliant recommendation creates an idempotent action intent; rejected or expired recommendations never reach a provider.

connections.label: Dry-run or provider mutation
connections.description: The executor rechecks provider state and preconditions, then invokes the correct adapter with an idempotency key and records the response for rollback review.

connections.label: Budget or recommendation notification
connections.description: Policy emits deduplicated notification intents for anomalies, budget risk, approval requests, and recommendation decisions without blocking ingestion.

connections.label: Action result
connections.description: Completed, failed, or partially applied provider actions generate an auditable notification and update the recommendation lifecycle.

connections.label: FinOps alert or approval prompt
connections.description: The notification service delivers configured email, chat, webhook, or ticket messages with provider response and deduplication status.

connections.label: Freshness and lag telemetry
connections.description: Monitoring compares provider watermarks with normalization and projection watermarks and alerts on missing accounts, lag, and replay gaps.

connections.label: Forecast and savings quality
connections.description: The engine reports forecast error, anomaly precision, recommendation acceptance, realized savings, model drift, and evidence completeness.

connections.label: Action safety telemetry
connections.description: Operations tracks approval bypass attempts, dry-run mismatches, provider throttling, mutation failures, rollback needs, and idempotency conflicts.

deepDives.title: Billing correctness and late data
points: For the multi-cloud FinOps platform, provider evidence, allocation coverage, model assumptions, and realized savings must remain distinguishable.

Design for the failure case where late billing, missing ownership, stale utilization, or an unsafe approval must not create a false saving or outage; keep retries, versions, and repair state explicit.
Expose freshness, version, lineage, or audit metadata so operators and clients can distinguish current, pending, and degraded state.

deepDives.title: Multi-cloud allocation and feature history
points: For the multi-cloud FinOps platform, provider evidence, allocation coverage, model assumptions, and realized savings must remain distinguishable.
Keep this concern off unrelated request paths and partition it by the multi-cloud FinOps platform access key.
Expose freshness, version, lineage, or audit metadata so operators and clients can distinguish current, pending, and degraded state.

tradeoffs.title: Raw lake plus serving index versus one database
tradeoffs.recommendation: Keep immutable provider evidence and canonical aggregates in durable analytical storage, with a separate tenant-filtered index for dashboards.
tradeoffs.caution: Two representations require watermarks and reconciliation, but a single database cannot serve billion-line-item history cheaply.

tradeoffs.title: Scheduled batch versus continuous analysis
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use provider-aligned batch ingestion for invoice-grade cost and a smaller streaming path for budget anomalies and action results.
tradeoffs.caution: Continuous polling hits provider quotas and creates false precision when billing data itself is delayed.

tradeoffs.title: Automatic remediation versus human approval
tradeoffs.recommendation: Automate low-risk detection and notification, but require policy, dry run, and scoped approval for production mutations or commitments.
tradeoffs.caution: Stale utilization, tags, or provider prices can turn automation into an outage or financial commitment.

commonMistakes: Treating provider APIs as a real-time invoice source.
Dropping credits, taxes, currency, amortization, shared costs, or reconciliation.
Generating recommendations without utilization evidence, confidence, model version, or freshness.
Letting an ML worker mutate resources without approval, dry run, and audit.
Scanning raw line items for every dashboard query or letting one account starve ingestion.

followUps.question: What happens when a provider revises a closed period?
followUps.answer: Land a new source version, reconcile it with the prior invoice, replay affected normalization and allocation partitions, and expose a correction watermark.

followUps.question: How do you prevent rightsizing from causing an outage?
followUps.answer: Require a confidence and utilization window, exclude protected resources, run a dry run, require approval, and recheck current state before mutation.

followUps.question: How do you verify savings are real?
followUps.answer: Record baseline and assumptions, then compare later provider usage and billing against a time-matched baseline and report realized savings separately.

rubric.description: The answer defines multi-cloud ingestion, invoice reconciliation, canonical allocation, explainable recommendations, approval safety, and realized savings, scale, latency, durability, authorization, and failure behavior.
Entities and keys make the multi-cloud FinOps platform state, versions, lifecycle, and derived projections explicit.
Partitioning, queues, backpressure, cache behavior, hot-key handling, and bounded work are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded behavior, observability, and auditability protect the primary contract.
The candidate can explain the multi-cloud FinOps platform consistency boundary, asynchronous work, and operational limits.
